question: Which is the MOST common presenting complaint of female genital tuberculosis in India?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Vaginal discharge is a common symptom of cervicitis and vaginitis (STIs, bacterial vaginosis) but is NOT the predominant presenting complaint of genital TB. The lower genital tract (vagina, cervix) is rarely the primary target in genital TB.

Correct. Infertility (primary or secondary) is the most common presenting complaint of genital TB in India, accounting for approximately 40–50% of female infertility in some series. The disease silently destroys the fallopian tubes over years before the woman seeks medical care for her inability to conceive.

Incorrect. While endometrial TB can occasionally cause abnormal uterine bleeding (including amenorrhoea or scanty menstruation from intrauterine adhesions/Asherman syndrome), postmenopausal bleeding is not a predominant presentation. Infertility is the cardinal complaint.

Incorrect. Genital TB is characteristically INSIDIOUS and SILENT — it does not typically present with acute pain and fever, which are more suggestive of acute PID or tubo-ovarian abscess. The silent, progressive nature of genital TB is why it so often presents only after irreversible damage has occurred.

overallFeedback.feedback: Genital TB is a SILENT disease. Infertility (primary or secondary) is the most common presentation — often the only complaint — because the fallopian tubes are the primary target and are destroyed long before symptoms appear.
Correct. Infertility is the hallmark presentation of genital TB. The disease silently destroys the tubes over years, which is why early detection is so difficult.
